races.name: Download The Raceday Ready App Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Merit Estates Chartered Surveyors Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Handicap

runners_data.name: Urban Road
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer with two places from five runs on Good ground at 10f; drops back to a flat mile here, which is sharper than recent assignments, and the visor headgear is retained — Ray Dawson has ridden it lately but the form string shows inconsistency, and it needs a fast-run race to pick up late.

runners_data.name: Glorious Kitty
runners_data.note: Arrives in cracking form with two wins from last three outings including a course victory at 8f Good; Lewis Chalkley claims 7lb and the Easterby yard has hit 5/35 in the past fortnight, making this a live each-way proposition who should travel prominently behind Poet's Dawn.

runners_data.name: Up The Jazz
runners_data.note: Won over 8f Good last time out and that form fits this race perfectly; Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim helps, and the Fahey yard is in fine form at 6/69 — this hold-up type has a strong record at this distance on this going and should be finishing with purpose from mid-division.

runners_data.name: Poet's Dawn
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the race and a two-time winner on Good ground at 9-10f; David Allan rides for Tim Easterby's in-form yard and the 11-year-old clearly retains ability — with no challenger for the lead, it has a significant tactical advantage that makes it dangerous despite advancing age.

runners_data.name: Popeye Doyle
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie applied and Jason Hart in the saddle for a yard that has sent out one winner from five recent runners; holds a second over 8f Good in recent form but has been disappointing since, and a flat mile at Ripon is an unexplored profile — needs others to make mistakes.

runners_data.name: Jesmond Dawn
runners_data.note: Strong recent form with two places from last three including a runner-up over 8f Good; only had three days' rest since its last run which merits monitoring — in truth a hold-up horse by nature but is mapped toward midfield here because the field is saturated with closers, which means it won't get the cleanest of late runs.

runners_data.name: Hopeful Joy
runners_data.note: Returns from a 45-day break for Mark Walford, whose yard has hit just 1/22 recently — the layoff is a concern even on a going it handles well; by inclination a closer, but with multiple hold-up types in the race it finds itself closer to the pace on the map than its natural style demands, limiting its margin for error.

runners_data.name: Precious Spartan
runners_data.note: Coming off an 89-day absence, the longest layoff in the field, which is a significant fitness query for Patrick Neville; its best form over 8f Good came a while ago and it hasn't won since — the redistribution into midfield reflects a field overstocked with closers, and freshness alone won't compensate for the lack of recent racing.

runners_data.name: Volenti
runners_data.note: Drops significantly in OR (51) compared to the field and is the bottom-weight in the race; a hold-up horse by nature whose last three runs at 8f Good have all yielded places without a win — Ben Haslam's yard is quiet at 1/17 recently, and while this horse is consistent it needs luck in running from a field this congested with similar types.

races.paceDynamic: Poet's Dawn is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a solo, uncontested gallop from the front over this flat Ripon mile on Good ground. The pace will be honest but controlled — Poet's Dawn has won twice at this trip and going combination and has every reason to bowl along at a rhythm that suits, rather than be pushed into a suicidal clip. Behind, Glorious Kitty is the most likely horse to press from a prominent pitch, with Urban Road and Up The Jazz likely to settle in behind before making their moves turning for home. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Jesmond Dawn, Hopeful Joy, Precious Spartan, and Volenti are all genuine closers who are redistributed toward midfield on the map, meaning their true closer's run is compromised by a race that may simply not generate enough late pace for them to pounce. This shape strongly favours horses who can track the leader prominently and sustain their effort into the final furlong — prominent racers and one-pace gallopers who can sit just off the controlled lead are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Poet's Dawn Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Poet's Dawn establishes an uncontested lead and maintains a measured gallop, no rival has the stomach to close.
scenarios.body: Poet's Dawn settles into a comfortable front-running rhythm on Good ground at a trip and surface where it has won twice; with no horse genuinely willing to chase it down, it simply extends approaching the final furlong and holds on. Glorious Kitty, tracking from second, is the most likely to mount a sustained challenge but must cope with a horse that has already stolen a march.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Wears Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Glorious Kitty or Up The Jazz tracks Poet's Dawn closely and outstays it inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A sustained gallop set by Poet's Dawn over a flat mile gradually plays into the hands of a horse sitting a length off the pace throughout; Glorious Kitty brings strong recent form (two wins from last three) and a jockey who can time a challenge, while Up The Jazz won over this exact trip and going last time out and is suited by a race run at this tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp Tiring Front-Runner
scenarios.trigger: If Poet's Dawn goes too fast early and the pace unravels in the final two furlongs, gifting a run to hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Urban Road and Jesmond Dawn are the pick of the closers if genuine late pace develops; however, multiple hold-up horses in this field are racing partially out of their natural role, which dilutes the chance that a clean late run materialises for any individual. Even in this scenario the redistribution of so many closers into midfield means they will race close enough to benefit if the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Midfield Scrimmage
scenarios.trigger: If several horses dispute prominent positions early, creating a rough race and neutralising Poet's Dawn's advantage.
scenarios.body: The clustering of redistributed hold-up types into midfield creates traffic complications on the turn; any horse that finds a clear run late could profit, but this scenario relies on the pace genuinely falling apart, which is unlikely given a lone confirmed front-runner setting an even tempo. Popeye Doyle with tongue-tie and Jason Hart could benefit from the chaos if rivals interfere with each other.

watchPoints.text: Poet's Dawn sets off uncontested — if David Allan controls the fractions, this horse could simply never be headed; monitor whether any rival attempts to go with it in the first two furlongs, as a fully unchallenged lead significantly increases its winning chance.

Glorious Kitty's jockey Lewis Chalkley is a 7lb claimer on a horse with two recent wins — if Chalkley can position it just off Poet's Dawn's quarters without using up Glorious Kitty's energy early, it becomes the most dangerous challenger in the race.

Hopeful Joy returns from a 45-day break and Precious Spartan from 89 days — both are closers already forced out of their natural role; if either shows any signs of ring-rustiness in the first half-mile, discount their chances completely in what is a strongly pace-scenario race.

Up The Jazz won over this exact trip and going last time out — watch for Warren Fentiman positioning it to travel smoothly in the first four furlongs; if it is still going well turning for home it represents the most straightforward form pick in the race.

The clustering of Jesmond Dawn, Hopeful Joy, Precious Spartan, and Volenti in midfield creates a congestion risk on the turn at Ripon — any horse drawn toward the inside that gets squeezed on the bend could lose all momentum; draw position and early positioning will matter.

races.name: Mark's Choice, Ripon's Most-Winning Horse Handicap

runners_data.name: Vince L'Amour
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 5yo has won at 5f on good ground before and races prominently, making this trip and conditions a fit; tongue tie returns and he arrives 18 days fresh, but his recent form string of 810067 shows inconsistency at this level.

runners_data.name: Tees Aggregates
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls-trained 4yo arrives in fine fettle off a 14-day break with a form string reading 945331 and a 5f-on-good record of 12/15 — a true hold-up type with powerful late speed who needs the pace to be honest enough to reel in.

runners_data.name: Rock Of England
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's 6yo is a hold-up specialist whose two recent wins have both come at 5f, and his 11/15 similar-going record underlines his aptitude; returns after 33 days but his trainer runs horses infrequently and they tend to be ready, so the layoff need not concern.

runners_data.name: Goyard
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 4yo is top-rated here on OR 82 and is the sole confirmed front-runner — Tudhope should get an uncontested lead, though his STYLE_FIT tag reflects that this is a horse capable of racing more freely than ideal; his form 1185-3 includes wins at 5f on good and softer ground.

runners_data.name: Kodiac Thriller
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's 5yo wears a visor and has a habit of racing prominently, but his last three runs at 6f on good or soft have been disappointing; the drop back to 5f is potentially helpful yet his form string of 7-0100 doesn't inspire confidence without a market move.

runners_data.name: Reigning Profit
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's veteran 7yo is a hold-up type on a quick turnaround of 11 days, with form reading 852046 — his 5f-on-good record of 9/15 is solid but he has not won recently and needs a stronger pace than this field is likely to generate to unleash his closing effort.

runners_data.name: Mark's Choice
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's 10yo is a genuine hold-up horse by nature, though the volume of similar types in this field has pushed him onto the map in midfield — at age 10 he retains ability as his 1-0624 form shows, but racing out of his preferred position with a STYLE_FIT discount tempers expectations; tongue strap noted.

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 6yo has a strong record of placing at 5f, including two recent wins, and races prominently — her 8/15 similar-going score suggests she handles good well enough, and tongue strap worn; arrives 19 days after her last run in solid nick and will be competitive in a race where prominent racers are favoured.

runners_data.name: South Parade
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's 5yo is a natural hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map due to the cluster of hold-up types in this field — his form of 000749 is modest and he has struggled to make an impact at this level recently, making the STYLE_FIT displacement a compounding issue rather than a minor one.

races.paceDynamic: Goyard is the one confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 5f handicap and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, Daniel Tudhope should be able to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than being dragged into a burning pace battle. Vince L'Amour and Canaria Queen will push to race prominently behind Goyard, giving the front of the field a compact three-horse pack, while Kodiac Thriller is also a prominent type who will be seeking to slot in just behind. Mark's Choice and South Parade are genuine hold-up horses by profile but, with the rear of the field already crowded with true hold-up types in Tees Aggregates, Rock Of England and Reigning Profit, they have been redistributed to midfield on the map — in reality they are unlikely to secure their natural position and may find themselves squeezed into a neither-here-nor-there berth. With one front-runner controlling a good-ground 5f at a measured clip, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race handy and sustain their effort throughout, or hold-up types with the acceleration to close a modest but steady gallop — prominent racers travelling within themselves off a sensible pace are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Goyard Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Goyard goes unchallenged to the front and sets a measured, uncontested gallop throughout the 5f.
scenarios.body: Tudhope dictates every yard at a pace that suits his mount, and the horses tracking just behind in a tight, compact group get the perfect opportunity to challenge in the final furlong without expending energy fighting for position early. Prominent horses racing within themselves off this pace are ideally placed to pounce close home on good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is quicker than it appears and the prominent horses are briefly stretched, leaving a gap for genuine hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Tees Aggregates and Rock Of England, both boasting excellent recent form at 5f on good ground, have the finishing speed to pick off weakening front-rank rivals if any fatigue sets in over the final furlong. Their strong similar-going records give confidence they handle these conditions, and both arrive in solid form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Weakens
scenarios.trigger: If Goyard is pushed wider or quicker than intended by early pressure from prominent rivals and the gallop becomes unsustainable.
scenarios.body: A fractionally stronger early pace would see the front-running types tied up inside the final furlong, handing the hold-up brigade more daylight than expected. Rock Of England and Tees Aggregates, both proven closers on this type of ground, would be the chief beneficiaries of any leader capitulating.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Defies Odds
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run in a chaotic or muddled fashion with no clear rhythm, scrambling the advantage of any single profile.
scenarios.body: South Parade or Mark's Choice, pushed out of their natural hold-up role and racing in unfamiliar midfield positions, could get a fortuitous passage if the race fragments and gaps open at the wrong time for fancied runners. At big prices either could sneak into frame money if chaos outweighs tactics, though their STYLE_FIT discount makes this a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch Goyard's price: if he drifts in the market despite holding the sole front-running role, it may signal that connections expect him to be slower away than usual and the prominent-racer advantage shifts to Vince L'Amour or Canaria Queen.

Monitor the draw at Ripon's 5f — low-drawn runners have an established advantage at this course and any prominent-style horse drawn high (particularly Kodiac Thriller or Vince L'Amour) will need to work harder to secure their position.

Tees Aggregates is a hold-up type arriving on a quick 14-day turnaround but with strong recent form (945331) — if the market shortens him significantly it suggests the Nicholls yard is bullish, and his closing speed on good ground makes him the primary danger to any front-rank horse.

Rock Of England's 33-day absence is notable given Paul Midgley's stable runs at 0/19 in the last 14 days — trainer not in form, so a market move or lack thereof will be informative before this race begins.

Both Mark's Choice and South Parade are true hold-up horses effectively racing out of their natural position — if the pace is as steady as expected, watch for either to be checked or short of room in the final two furlongs, making them unreliable at any price.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap

runners_data.name: Picaro
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse who needs a genuine pace to close into; trainer James Owen sends him back 25 days after a fourth on Soft-ish ground, but the similarity-going record reads 0 wins and 0 places from four runs and the lack of any front-runner here is a significant tactical problem.

runners_data.name: Vietnorm
runners_data.note: Three recent wins on Good ground over 10f-16f make this the standout form profile for the race shape; Barry McHugh rides a horse who clearly handles today's conditions and trip, and the hat-trick of wins gives strong confidence that he is in form, though a 37-day break (24 since jockey booking) is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Fairydale
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old wears a hood and has a placed effort over this exact trip on Good ground from five runs back; naturally a hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot here because so many closers contest this race, which tempers confidence that she can reproduce that placed effort cleanly.

runners_data.name: Keep It Classic
runners_data.note: William Haggas sends a three-year-old who has placed at 12f on Good ground twice and wears a tongue-tie; his natural instinct is to come from behind, but the overcrowded hold-up division means he may end up closer to the pace than usual — a role that suits his form profile if the gallop is genuine.

runners_data.name: Resdev Time
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's gelding is the freshest runner on 13 days, wears a hood, and has a solid record of 7 runs on Good going from 10 runs overall; genuinely a hold-up type reassigned to midfield due to the crowd at the rear, and a STYLE_FIT tag means discount his chance if this shape demands the far-back position.

runners_data.name: Hansteen
runners_data.note: Carries a notable fitness concern after 89 days off and is tagged as fading in the finish, which is alarming in a race with no pace to soften rivals; John & Sean Quinn's three-year-old has only three runs to show and just one on Good ground, making him the most uncertain commodity in the field.

runners_data.name: Star Of Emerald
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's three-year-old is the only runner with an unknown style tag, making her the wild card for the pace map; her recent fourth over 12f on Good ground is arguably the most relevant form to today, and if she drifts forward and controls the race she could prove very dangerous.

runners_data.name: Riddikulus
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's three-year-old wears blinkers, has shown consistency in placing at 14f on Soft and 10f on Good, and apprentice Rhys Elliott claims 5lbs; the horse is a natural hold-up type crowded into midfield by the field's composition, meaning the style discount applies, though the combination of headgear and weight advantage keeps him involved at longer prices.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field, Ripon's 1m4f trip is set to be run at an uncertain, likely modest gallop with no horse willing to commit hard from the front. Star Of Emerald is the one runner with an unknown style profile who could drift forward and set the tempo, but if she settles back the field risks crawling into a bunched sprint finish over the last two furlongs. The field is dominated by hold-up types — Vietnorm, Picaro, Fairydale, Keep It Classic, Resdev Time, Hansteen, and Riddikulus all want to come from behind, meaning the race is almost certain to compress into a late dash with little meaningful pace to stretch it out. This shape strongly favours the horse with the highest cruising speed and the cleanest late kick, rewarding a horse who can travel sweetly in midfield and produce a decisive, well-timed finish — Vietnorm's three recent wins at this trip on Good ground makes that profile extremely relevant. The field holds more hold-up types than can all settle at the rear naturally; among those redistributed to midfield, Keep It Classic and Fairydale are most likely to edge forward and occupy a closer position than their true style dictates.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow pace sprint finish
scenarios.trigger: If no horse commits to the lead and the field crawls into a bunched final-furlong dash
scenarios.body: With an absence of genuine pace-setters, the race drifts into a sprint finish where superior finishing speed and good ground form at this trip prove decisive; Vietnorm's hat-trick of wins over 10f-16f on Good ground makes him the standout profile here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady pace stamina test
scenarios.trigger: If Star Of Emerald or another runner edges forward to set a gentle, measured tempo that rewards the most resolute stayer
scenarios.body: A controlled but genuine gallop stretches the field gradually in the straight, rewarding horses who stay well rather than those relying on a sharp finishing burst; Vietnorm's proven stamina at 16f on Good ground and Keep It Classic's placed run at 12f on Good both suit this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer fails to get through
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed field creates traffic problems and pace-pressers who tracked slightly closer grab the initiative in the straight
scenarios.body: With so many true hold-up horses competing for the same late ground, those who can travel closer to the pace in the midfield group benefit from fewer rivals to pass; Keep It Classic and Fairydale, though natural hold-up types likely to find themselves slightly more prominent than intended, could capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lone traveller steals it
scenarios.trigger: If one horse, most likely Star Of Emerald, unexpectedly takes up a clear lead early and is allowed to stride away unchallenged at a true gallop
scenarios.body: A solo front-runner left unchallenged on Good ground over 1m4f at Ripon can set a fractions-controlled pace and be very hard to reel in from a field full of sluggish starters; Star Of Emerald's unknown style and recent return to form over 12f make her the likeliest beneficiary if the field is slow to respond.

watchPoints.text: Vietnorm's three-win streak on Good ground over this trip and further makes him the one horse whose profile perfectly matches the likely slow-pace sprint finish — watch if Barry McHugh can get a clear run from the hold-up group.

Star Of Emerald is the only horse with an unknown style in this field; if Rowan Scott elects to send her forward early and the others are slow to react, she could control proceedings and drastically change the race shape from expected.

Traffic risk is high with six or seven horses all wanting late positions in a small eight-runner field — watch the straight carefully for Picaro, Riddikulus, and Resdev Time becoming boxed in behind rivals who are also trying to close.

Hansteen is 89 days off the track with only three career runs and a pattern of fading in the finish — if he struggles for fitness in the straight, he could block the run of closer rivals behind him, making him a positioning hazard.

Keep It Classic's trainer William Haggas and Tom Marquand are a high-class combination dropping well down in class; the horse may find himself unexpectedly prominent given the redistribution dynamic, and that closer position could suit him better than his natural style suggests.

races.name: David Chapman Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Mare Of London
runners_data.note: A hold-up filly with a solid second on good ground at 6f among her recent efforts; 306 days off the track is a significant concern and Ray Dawson will need to find a clear run late if the pace is as slow as expected.

runners_data.name: Lamlash Bay
runners_data.note: Only 10 days since her last run and naturally prominent, Lewis Chalkley (7lb claim) is best placed to press Brash and make this a genuine two-horse lead contest; her soft-ground run suggests stamina is not the issue but her 14th-of-14 on good ground at 6f last season is a red flag.

runners_data.name: Soul Warrior
runners_data.note: Won on soft at 6f but has finished no closer than eighth in three good-ground starts; his natural inclination is to be held up at the back and he is one of several true closers squeezed into a midfield position by the sheer volume of hold-up types in this field — his finish-fading habit on good is a concern.

runners_data.name: Brash
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and the axis around which this entire race revolves; David Barron's three-year-old has finished outside the places in all three starts but an uncontested lead at Ripon on good is a completely different opportunity, and Oisin Orr's experience is the key booking.

runners_data.name: Hvar
runners_data.note: His sole win came at Southwell on standard going and he has finished tailed off or well beaten in six of seven starts on turf; John & Sean Quinn's runner is a genuine hold-up type for whom a slowly-run 6f on a flat straight is close to worst case.

runners_data.name: Tie Fighter
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides and the blinkers are on for the first time; two placed efforts at 6f on standard going suggest Dunlop's three-year-old has ability, but his soft-ground form dominates the record and getting involved from a midfield position suits him better than a slow-run chase.

runners_data.name: Northern Tempest
runners_data.note: Three top-four finishes at 6f on good give him the most relevant form in the field for today's conditions; tongue-tie fitted and Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim helps at the weights, though his true racing style is at the back and he has been squeezed into a midfield slot by the density of hold-up horses — he will need to be ridden more forwardly than ideal.

runners_data.name: Havana Oaks
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's filly has only three runs to assess and all on softer or standard ground, so today's good going is an unknown; she belongs at the back of the field naturally but the crowded hold-up group means Barry McHugh may be forced to find cover in midfield instead.

runners_data.name: Long Shot
runners_data.note: The most consistent horse in the race with three placed finishes on good ground at this trip; David Allan has experience placing horses from off the pace and the tongue-tie plus hood combination (hg:p) suggests connections are searching for improvement, though a slow pace set by Brash is the biggest obstacle to his finishing run materialising.

races.paceDynamic: Brash is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to push the tempo, Oisin Orr can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on this straight 6f Ripon track. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly made up of hold-up types — Soul Warrior, Northern Tempest, Havana Oaks, Long Shot and Hvar all want to come from off the pace — meaning the race will likely be run at a measured rhythm that keeps Brash fresh into the final two furlongs rather than blowing him away. Lamlash Bay is the only runner with a genuine prominent profile and may attempt to press Brash, but with limited recent form to suggest she can go with him, the pace dynamic remains thin. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the track can accommodate in true rear-running positions; Lamlash Bay is best placed to secure a prominent berth alongside Brash, while Soul Warrior and Northern Tempest — both genuine closers — are the most likely to find space off the pace, though their redistribution to midfield on the map reflects how crowded the back of the field will be. This race shape — a single unhurried front-runner on a flat, straight course with a wall of hold-up types behind — strongly favours horses who can race prominently or make a smooth, early move from midfield, as a slow-run 6f at Ripon rarely produces a true late-flying finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Brash Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lamlash Bay fails to press Brash early and the pace remains slow-to-moderate, allowing Brash to control every yard.
scenarios.body: Brash dictates a comfortable gallop and Oisin Orr can nurse him to the two-furlong pole before kicking for home, leaving the hold-up brigade with too little ground to make up. A slow pace on this flat track hands a decisive advantage to the horse who gets a clean lead and builds momentum gradually — Brash is that horse.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Lamlash Bay tracks Brash closely throughout and the pace is slightly hotter than expected, setting up a duel.
scenarios.body: Brash and Lamlash Bay match strides down the straight with both jockeys committed early, leaving the winner likely to be whichever has the superior late reserves. Tie Fighter and Mare Of London, with the ability to sit just off the pace in a rhythm, could pick up the pieces if both leaders empty.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to stop the front-runner and a midfield horse produces a sustained run from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Northern Tempest or Long Shot — both genuine hold-up horses with course-relevant form — would need a stronger gallop than Brash is likely to set, but if Lamlash Bay does force the tempo, a late surge becomes conceivable. Long Shot's three placed efforts at this trip on good ground give this scenario its only meaningful traction, though the redistribution of true closers to midfield means many of these runners will be racing too close to the pace to finish with a true flourish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swamp Them
scenarios.trigger: If the race descends into chaos, with several jockeys gambling on a late run simultaneously in a falsely-run race.
scenarios.body: With four or five genuine hold-up horses all waiting for a gap that never fully opens, most will find themselves checked or short of room in the final furlong. Hvar's one win came from the back at Southwell on standard, making Good ground and a flat Ripon straight a different ask; only a rider prepared to commit earlier than their natural style dictates stands any chance.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Lamlash Bay's Lewis Chalkley (7) attempts to press Brash from the outset — if he does not, Brash will control an uncontested lead and the race shape is effectively sealed inside the first furlong.

Monitor the draw and early positioning of Long Shot and Northern Tempest: if both are forced to race genuinely wide or are boxed behind a wall of hold-up types, their already-uncertain late runs become near-impossible on a flat track with no bend to create gaps.

Soul Warrior's record of fading in finishes on good ground combined with being pushed out of his natural rear-running position means he could drop away tamely — flag him as a possible fader rather than a closer in running.

Hvar's tailed-off runs on turf good ground and his sole win being on Southwell standard make him a potential non-factor; Jason Hart may be forced to commit earlier than normal to avoid getting swamped, which would be entirely against the horse's profile.

Tie Fighter wears blinkers for the first time today — watch whether the headgear sharpens him out of the gate and allows Tom Marquand to secure a midfield position closer to the pace than his recent races suggest, which would significantly change his chance in a slowly-run race.
